newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Irish president to visit Bosnia tribunal Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Irish president to visit Bosnia tribunal Wednesday.

text.p: President of Ireland Mary Robinson is to visit the U.N. criminal tribunal for former Yugoslavia on Wednesday, a tribunal spokesman said on Tuesday.

"Tomorrow morning the beginning of the procedings will be delayed for about 15-20 minutes because Mrs Mary Robinson, the president of Ireland, will be paying the first ever visit by a head of state," said tribunal spokesman Christian Chartier.
Robinson, herself a prominent lawyer, will meet tribunal president Antonio Cassese, chief prosecutor Louise Arbour and six trial judges, he added.

"The purpose of the visit is to confirm the support of the tribunal by Ireland," as well as to give Robinson the opportunity to demonstrate her personal attachment to human rights issues, said Chartier.
The tribunal is currently trying four men, three Moslems and one Croat, for war crimes at the Celebici camp in central Bosnia in 1992.

As of March 3, 1996 the tribunal had indicted 75 suspects -- 54 Serbs (one of whom has since died), 18 Croats and three Moslems. One man has been convicted and sentenced to 10 years in jail, a verdict is expected soon in another case. Another man is in the tribunal's 24-cell detention centre awaiting trial.
The two most prominent indicted suspects are former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and former Bosnian Serb military commander Ratko Mladic, both of whom remain at large.
